steps.say: This is Winnipeg Parcel Search, the city companion to the Manitoba tool. It uses the City's open data for parcels, assessment, zoning and neighbourhoods. In this video we find a property, read its popup, and export the result.
Type a civic number and the street name. The street box suggests matches as you type, so you can pick one from the list or just press Enter to search.
With both From and To filled, the search is exact. One number alone is a contains match and would return every address containing it.
Click the parcel on the map for a popup. The click popup has Copy Roll and G P S Coordinates links, and goes straight to the assessment page.
Roll numbers go in the chip box. Enter or a comma adds a chip, and the search accepts rolls with or without dashes and leading zeros. Here is the same parcel by roll.
The address box on the map itself is another way in. Type an address, pick it from the list, and the search fields fill and run.
Column presets switch the table between quick lookup, residential, zoning detail, sales, and full detail. The gear builds a custom set. Click a header to sort.
Search a whole street for every parcel on it. Border Street gives a couple of dozen. Untick rows to drop them from the map, the charts and the export without searching again.
Export C S V writes the table as shown. If rows are unticked, it asks first. The title at the top left is a home button that clears everything.
